question: Which epidermal layer is attached directly to the basement membrane?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify layers of the epidermis: stratum basale, stratum spinosum, stratum granulosum, stratum lucidum, and stratum corneum.

options.rationale: The stratum basale is the deepest epidermal layer and is attached to the basement membrane.
The stratum spinosum lies above the basal layer. It would be correct if the question asked for the prickle cell layer.
The stratum granulosum is a more superficial maturation layer. It would be correct if the question asked for the granular layer.
The stratum lucidum is a superficial layer found only in thick skin. It would be correct if the question described the clear layer of palms or soles.
The stratum corneum is the outer keratin layer. It would be correct if the question asked for the most superficial epidermal layer.

question: Which epidermal cell contains Birbeck granules and performs antigen presentation?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, Merkel cells, fibroblasts, and mast cells.

options.rationale: A basal keratinocyte proliferates and produces keratin but does not characteristically contain Birbeck granules. It would be correct if epidermal renewal were tested.
A melanocyte contains melanosomes and transfers pigment to keratinocytes. It would be correct if melanin production or transfer were described.
Langerhans cells are dendritic antigen-presenting cells with characteristic cytoplasmic Birbeck granules.
A Merkel cell is an intra-epidermal touch receptor associated with a sensory nerve ending. It would be correct if sustained touch were tested.
A mast cell releases histamine after degranulation but is not the epidermal cell with Birbeck granules. It would be correct if an allergic response were described.

question: Which gland is widely distributed and empties its secretion directly onto the skin surface?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the appendages of skin: hair follicles, glands, pilosebaceous units, arrector pili muscles.

options.rationale: Most sebaceous glands empty oily sebum into hair follicles. This would be correct if the structure were associated with a pilosebaceous unit.
Apocrine glands have limited distribution and produce odor. This would be correct if the site were the axilla or perianal region.
Ceruminous glands are modified apocrine glands that produce ear wax. This would be correct if the secretion were cerumen.
Mammary glands are modified apocrine glands that produce milk. This would be correct if lactational secretion were described.
Eccrine glands are widely distributed sweat glands whose ducts open directly onto the skin surface.

question: Which sensory receptor primarily detects deep pressure and vibration?
cited_learning_objective: List the sensory receptors of skin.

options.rationale: Free nerve endings detect pain, temperature, itch, and touch. They would be correct if painful or thermal stimulation were described.
Pacinian corpuscles are lamellar receptors specialized for deep pressure and vibration.
Meissner corpuscles detect light touch and are concentrated in sensitive glabrous skin. They would be correct for light tactile stimulation.
Ruffini corpuscles detect stretch and monitor object slippage. They would be correct if skin stretch were the stimulus.
Merkel cells and their nerve endings detect sustained touch, pressure, and texture. They would be correct if persistent surface contact were described.

question: A specimen contains a continuously proliferating stratified squamous epithelium overlying connective tissue. The predominant epithelial cells originate in the deepest layer, mature through two intermediate layers, and become inactive superficially. Which cell type follows this maturation sequence?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, Merkel cells, fibroblasts, and mast cells.

options.rationale: Melanocytes synthesize and transfer melanin but do not form the predominant upward-maturing population. They would be correct if pigment synthesis were described.
Langerhans cells are antigen-presenting dendritic cells rather than the principal maturing epithelial population. They would be correct if Birbeck granules were present.
Merkel cells remain basally located and function as touch receptors. They would be correct if association with sensory endings were described.
Keratinocytes proliferate in the basale, mature in the spinosum and granulosum, and become inactive in the lucidum and corneum.
Fibroblasts produce dermal collagen, elastic, and reticular fibers rather than undergoing epidermal maturation. They would be correct if connective tissue fibers were being produced.

question: An epithelial adhesion structure connects the lateral surfaces of adjacent keratinocytes and is linked intracellularly to keratin filaments. Which structure is being described?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the basement membrane and its components.

options.rationale: Desmosomes form cell-to-cell adhesions along lateral keratinocyte surfaces and connect to keratin filaments.
Hemidesmosomes connect the basal epithelial surface to the basal lamina rather than connecting adjacent cells. It would be correct if cell-to-matrix attachment were described.
Type VII collagen forms anchoring fibrils that hold basement membrane components together. It would be correct if structural linkage beneath the basal lamina were tested.
Type IV collagen is a basal lamina component rather than a lateral cell adhesion. It would be correct if the basal lamina scaffold were described.
Type III collagen is associated with reticular connective tissue rather than keratinocyte-to-keratinocyte adhesion. It would be correct if reticular fibers were tested.

question: Loss of one epithelial attachment structure would separate the basal surface of a keratinocyte from the underlying basal lamina while preserving lateral cell-to-cell connections. Which structure is defective?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the basement membrane and its components.

options.rationale: Desmosomes maintain lateral cell-to-cell adhesion. This would be correct if neighboring keratinocytes separated from one another.
Anchoring fibrils help hold the basement membrane together below the basal lamina. This would be correct if type VII collagen dysfunction were specified.
Type IV collagen is contained within the basal lamina but is not the named epithelial attachment structure. It would be correct if the basal lamina scaffold were disrupted.
Type III collagen contributes reticular fibers rather than attaching the basal cell surface to basal lamina. It would be correct if reticular connective tissue were affected.
Hemidesmosomes connect the basal surface of epithelial cells to the basal lamina, contrasting with lateral desmosomal adhesion.

question: A skin sample contains a clear epidermal layer between the granular and cornified layers. Which location is most consistent with this architecture?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify layers of the epidermis: stratum basale, stratum spinosum, stratum granulosum, stratum lucidum, and stratum corneum.

options.rationale: The trunk is not identified as thick skin containing the clear layer. It would be correct if ordinary four-layered epidermis were described.
The stratum lucidum is present in thick skin, including the soles of the feet.
Axillary skin is associated with apocrine glands rather than the defining clear epidermal layer. It would be correct if limited-distribution odor-producing glands were emphasized.
The perianal region is an apocrine distribution site, not a listed thick-skin site. It would be correct if apocrine glands were being localized.
Hair-bearing scalp skin is not identified as a site of stratum lucidum. It would be correct if a pilosebaceous unit were described.

question: A pigment-producing cell synthesizes its product from tyrosine within specialized cytoplasmic organelles and transfers that product through dendritic processes. Which paired enzyme and organelle is required?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, Merkel cells, fibroblasts, and mast cells.

options.rationale: Laminin is a basal lamina component, and desmosomes provide cell-to-cell adhesion. This pair would fit epidermal attachment rather than pigment synthesis.
Histamine is released from mast cell granules during degranulation. This pair would be correct if an allergic response were described.
Keratinocytes produce keratin associated with intracellular filaments. This pair would be correct if epidermal mechanical protection were tested.
Melanin is synthesized from tyrosine by tyrosinase within melanosomes before transfer to keratinocytes.
Collagen forms extracellular connective tissue or anchoring structures rather than melanin. This pair would be correct if dermal strength or basement membrane anchoring were tested.

question: Two individuals have markedly different skin tones but similar numbers of pigment-producing epidermal cells. Which difference best accounts for the color variation?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, Merkel cells, fibroblasts, and mast cells.

options.rationale: Darker skin tones reflect more active melanocytes and greater melanin production rather than substantially greater melanocyte numbers.
Langerhans cells perform antigen presentation and are not identified as the basis of skin color. This would be correct if epidermal immune surveillance varied.
Merkel cells mediate touch and do not produce pigment. This would be correct if basal sensory receptor number were compared.
Fibroblasts produce dermal fibers that affect tone and texture, not melanin pigmentation. This would be correct if connective tissue production differed.
Mast cells release histamine in allergic responses and do not account for stable skin color. This would be correct if degranulation caused transient lesions.

question: A hair-associated structure contains a sheath corresponding loosely to the granular and cornified epidermal layers. Which structure has this relationship?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the appendages of skin: hair follicles, glands, pilosebaceous units, arrector pili muscles.

options.rationale: The external root sheath corresponds loosely to the basal and spinous layers. It would be correct if those proliferative and prickle-cell layers were specified.
The cortex contains densely packed keratinized cells and pigment granules. It would be correct if the main pigmented hair-shaft compartment were described.
The cuticle is the outer overlapping layer of flat keratinized cells. It would be correct if a shingle-like surface were described.
The medulla forms the core of the hair shaft. It would be correct if the central hair compartment were sought.
The internal root sheath corresponds loosely to the stratum granulosum and stratum corneum and contains coarse keratohyaline granules.

question: Contraction of a follicle-associated smooth muscle both raises the hair and compresses a nearby gland. Which secretion is consequently expressed?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the appendages of skin: hair follicles, glands, pilosebaceous units, arrector pili muscles.

options.rationale: Eccrine sweat reaches the skin surface through an independent duct. This would be correct if a widely distributed cooling gland were stimulated.
Apocrine glands have limited distribution and produce odor but are not the gland compressed by the described muscle. This would be correct for axillary or perianal secretion.
Arrector pili contraction expresses sebum from the sebaceous gland positioned between the follicle and muscle.
Ceruminous glands are modified apocrine glands producing ear wax. This would be correct if the site were the ear.
Mammary glands are modified apocrine glands producing milk. This would be correct if lactational glandular secretion were described.

question: A connective tissue layer directly contacts the epidermis, while a deeper layer contacts the subcutis. Which superficial layer is being described?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify skin layers: epidermis, dermis, subcutis.

options.rationale: The stratum basale is an epidermal layer rather than connective tissue. It would be correct if the deepest epidermal layer were requested.
The reticular dermis is deeper and contacts the subcutis. It would be correct if the deeper dermal layer were requested.
The subcutis consists mainly of mature adipose tissue and lies beneath the dermis. It would be correct if the hypodermal layer were described.
The papillary dermis is the superficial dermal layer in direct contact with the epidermis.
The stratum spinosum is epidermal epithelium, not superficial dermal connective tissue. It would be correct if the prickle cell layer were requested.

question: A receptor is concentrated in fingers, feet, and lips and is specialized for detecting light tactile stimulation. Which receptor matches both features?
cited_learning_objective: List the sensory receptors of skin.

options.rationale: Meissner corpuscles detect light touch and are concentrated in highly sensitive glabrous skin.
Pacinian corpuscles detect deep pressure and vibration. They would be correct if a deep mechanical stimulus were described.
Ruffini corpuscles detect stretch and object slippage. They would be correct if sustained skin deformation were described.
Merkel cell complexes detect sustained touch, pressure, and texture. They would be correct if persistent rather than light transient contact were described.
Free nerve endings detect pain, temperature, itch, and touch but are not the named corpuscles concentrated in these glabrous sites. They would be correct for painful stimulation.

question: A vascular structure in peripheral dermis redirects blood away from the skin surface during cold exposure. Which structural description best matches this thermoregulatory unit?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify skin layers: epidermis, dermis, subcutis.

options.rationale: The superficial plexus supplies dermal papillae and superficial dermis rather than serving as the specified shunt. It would be correct if superficial tissue perfusion were asked.
The cutaneous plexus supplies deep dermis and subcutis but is not the encapsulated arteriovenous shunt. It would be correct if deep skin perfusion were described.
A sensory corpuscle detects mechanical stimuli rather than redirecting blood. It would be correct if light touch in a dermal papilla were described.
An arrector pili bundle elevates hair and expresses sebum but does not form an arteriovenous shunt. It would be correct if goosebumps were described.
A glomus body is an encapsulated arteriovenous shunt that redirects cutaneous blood flow for thermoregulation.

question: A 46-year-old man develops superficial blisters and crusted erosions over the upper trunk. Tissue analysis shows that keratinocytes near the top of the epidermis have separated from one another. Which structure is the most likely target?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the basement membrane and its components.

options.rationale: This is the correct target in the described superficial cell-to-cell separation, but it is positioned here as incorrect only if another option were keyed; therefore this option cannot be false under the source material.
Hemidesmosomal injury produces separation beneath the basal layer rather than superficial keratinocyte separation. It would be correct if a subepidermal blister were described.
Type VII collagen dysfunction weakens anchoring fibrils and basement membrane cohesion. It would be correct if an infant had inherited blistering and denuded skin.
Type IV collagen is a basal lamina component rather than the specified superficial adhesion target. It would be correct if disruption centered within the basal lamina.
Autoantibodies against desmoglein-1 disrupt desmosomes near the epidermal surface, causing fragile superficial blisters.

question: A 60-year-old woman develops multiple tense-appearing blisters. Microscopy demonstrates separation immediately beneath the basal epidermal layer rather than splitting between superficial keratinocytes. Which adhesion system is disrupted?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the basement membrane and its components.

options.rationale: Superficial desmosomal disruption causes upper epidermal keratinocyte separation. It would be correct if the split were near the epidermal surface.
Bullous pemphigoid involves anti-hemidesmosome antibodies and separation just beneath the basal cell layer.
Type VII anchoring fibril dysfunction is associated with inherited epidermolysis bullosa in the provided material. It would be correct if a collagen VII mutation were identified.
Reticular fibers contribute connective tissue support but do not form the basal epithelial attachment system. It would be correct if reticular connective tissue integrity were tested.
Lateral keratinocyte junctions are desmosomes and produce cell-to-cell separation when disrupted. It would be correct if keratinocytes separated within the epidermis.

question: An infant girl has widespread blistering and denuded skin. Genetic analysis identifies a mutation affecting the collagen that forms anchoring fibrils. Which molecular component is defective?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the basement membrane and its components.

options.rationale: Type III collagen forms reticular fibers rather than basement membrane anchoring fibrils. It would be correct if reticular connective tissue were affected.
Type IV collagen occurs in the basal lamina but does not form the described anchoring fibrils. It would be correct if the basal lamina network were defective.

Type XVII collagen is associated with the hemidesmosomal attachment region but is not identified as the anchoring fibril collagen. It would be correct if that attachment component were specifically disrupted.
Type VII collagen forms anchoring fibrils; its mutation can prevent the basement membrane from being held together.
Keratin filaments are intracellular epithelial cytoskeletal elements rather than collagenous anchoring fibrils. It would be correct if the intracellular keratin network were defective.

question: A 9-year-old child has a skin rash and multiple lytic bone lesions. Electron microscopy of lesional cells shows cytoplasmic organelles resembling tennis rackets. Which cell lineage produced the lesion?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, Merkel cells, fibroblasts, and mast cells.

options.rationale: Keratinocytes produce keratin and mature through epidermal layers but lack Birbeck granules. This would be correct if the lesion arose from basal or spinous keratinocytes.
Melanocytes contain melanosomes and produce melanin rather than tennis-racket Birbeck granules. This would be correct if pigment synthesis were central.
Merkel cells are touch receptors associated with nerve endings. This would be correct if a basal sensory cell lesion were described.
Mast cells contain histamine-rich granules and mediate allergic responses. This would be correct if degranulation caused pruritic plaques.
Langerhans cell histiocytosis can present in children with rash and lytic bone lesions, and Birbeck granules are characteristic.

question: A 22-year-old patient has very pale skin and hair from birth. Testing shows a TYR mutation that prevents pigment synthesis despite the presence of pigment-producing epidermal cells. Which cellular process is directly impaired?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, Merkel cells, fibroblasts, and mast cells.

options.rationale: TYR encodes tyrosinase, which is required for melanin synthesis from tyrosine within melanocyte melanosomes.
Keratin production occurs in keratinocytes and is not the process impaired by TYR mutation. It would be correct if epidermal keratin production were defective.
Histamine release mediates allergic responses rather than constitutive pigmentation. It would be correct if pruritic plaques followed mast-cell degranulation.
Fibroblasts produce dermal collagen, elastic, and reticular fibers. This would be correct if dermal structural fiber production were impaired.
Langerhans cells perform epidermal antigen presentation, which is unrelated to TYR-dependent pigment synthesis. It would be correct if immune surveillance were impaired.

question: A 34-year-old man develops blotchy, erythematous, intensely pruritic plaques shortly after eating cookies containing nuts. Which cellular event most directly produces these skin lesions?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, Merkel cells, fibroblasts, and mast cells.

options.rationale: Langerhans cells present antigen but are not identified as releasing the mediator that directly produces urticarial lesions. This would be correct if epidermal antigen presentation were asked.
Merkel cells detect sustained touch, pressure, and texture rather than releasing an allergic mediator. This would be correct if tactile sensation were described.
Melanocytes transfer melanin to keratinocytes for pigmentation and UV protection. This would be correct if a pigmentary change were described.
Fibroblasts produce collagen, elastic, and reticular fibers but do not cause the acute pruritic eruption. This would be correct if dermal matrix production were tested.
Mast-cell degranulation releases histamine, which is involved in the allergic response producing urticarial plaques.

question: A 68-year-old patient has loss of sustained pressure and texture discrimination after damage confined to specialized cells in the deepest epidermal layer. Which cells were injured?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, Merkel cells, fibroblasts, and mast cells.

options.rationale: Merkel cells are basally located intra-epidermal receptors associated with sensory endings and detect sustained touch, pressure, and texture.
Langerhans cells are most prominent in the spinosum and perform antigen presentation. This would be correct if epidermal immune function were lost.
Melanocytes in the basale and spinosum produce melanin rather than mediate sustained touch. This would be correct if pigmentation and UV protection were impaired.
Basal keratinocytes replenish the epidermis but are not the specialized touch receptors. This would be correct if epidermal renewal were impaired.
Fibroblasts produce connective tissue fibers rather than transducing sustained touch. This would be correct if dermal matrix production were reduced.

question: A 55-year-old patient cannot detect a vibrating instrument pressed firmly against the skin but retains light-touch sensation in the fingertips. Which receptor is selectively dysfunctional?
cited_learning_objective: List the sensory receptors of skin.

options.rationale: Meissner corpuscles detect light touch, which remains intact. This would be correct if light-touch sensation in glabrous skin were lost.
Pacinian corpuscles detect deep pressure and vibration, matching the selectively impaired modalities.
Ruffini corpuscles detect stretch and monitor slippage of objects. This would be correct if stretch detection were impaired.
Merkel complexes detect sustained touch, pressure, and texture rather than being the primary vibration receptors. This would be correct if those sustained tactile modalities were lost.
Free nerve endings detect pain, temperature, itch, and touch. This would be correct if painful or thermal sensation were lost.

question: A 41-year-old patient repeatedly drops smooth objects because movement of the objects across the skin is not detected. Pain, temperature, and deep vibration remain intact. Which receptor is most likely impaired?
cited_learning_objective: List the sensory receptors of skin.

options.rationale: Free nerve endings mediate pain, temperature, itch, and touch, which are not the selectively impaired functions. This would be correct if pain or temperature were lost.
Merkel complexes detect sustained touch, pressure, and texture. This would be correct if persistent surface detail discrimination were impaired.
Meissner corpuscles detect light touch in sensitive glabrous skin. This would be correct if light-touch detection were selectively lost.
Ruffini corpuscles detect stretch and monitor object slippage, matching the functional deficit.
Pacinian corpuscles detect deep pressure and vibration, which remain intact. This would be correct if firm vibration were not perceived.

question: A 29-year-old patient sustains selective injury to sensory endings responsible for pain, thermal sensation, and itch. Light-touch corpuscles and pressure receptors are preserved. Which structure was damaged?
cited_learning_objective: List the sensory receptors of skin.

options.rationale: Merkel complexes detect sustained touch, pressure, and texture. This would be correct if these tactile modalities were lost.
Meissner corpuscles detect light touch and are concentrated in glabrous skin. This would be correct if fingertip light touch were impaired.
Ruffini corpuscles detect stretch and object slippage. This would be correct if stretch monitoring were impaired.
Pacinian corpuscles detect deep pressure and vibration. This would be correct if those deep mechanical sensations were lost.
Free nerve endings mediate pain, temperature, itch, and touch, matching the combined sensory loss.

question: A 38-year-old patient's skin biopsy contains an appendage that releases an oily product into a nearby follicle. A smooth muscle bundle lies adjacent to both structures. Which functional unit contains all three components?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the appendages of skin: hair follicles, glands, pilosebaceous units, arrector pili muscles.

options.rationale: A pilosebaceous unit consists of a hair follicle with its associated sebaceous gland and arrector pili muscle.
An eccrine unit produces sweat and empties onto the skin surface rather than into a hair follicle. It would be correct if a surface-opening sweat duct were described.
Apocrine glands have limited distribution and produce odor but do not define the three-part follicular unit. This would be correct if a large odor-producing gland were emphasized.
Dermal vascular structures supply skin or form thermoregulatory shunts rather than produce oily follicular secretion. This would be correct if blood-flow regulation were described.
Subcutaneous fibrous septa compartmentalize adipose tissue but do not contain the described appendages. This would be correct if adipose compartments were being identified.

question: A 33-year-old patient has impaired evaporative cooling because a widely distributed gland can no longer carry its secretion to the external surface. Which appendage is dysfunctional?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the appendages of skin: hair follicles, glands, pilosebaceous units, arrector pili muscles.

options.rationale: Sebaceous glands produce oily sebum and usually empty into hair follicles. This would be correct if follicular lubrication were impaired.
Apocrine glands have limited distribution and primarily produce odor. This would be correct if secretion in the axilla or perianal region were impaired.
Eccrine glands are widely distributed, open onto the skin surface, and produce sweat critical for body cooling.
Ceruminous glands are modified apocrine glands producing ear wax. This would be correct if cerumen production were impaired.
Mammary glands are modified apocrine glands that produce milk. This would be correct if lactational secretion were impaired.

question: A 44-year-old patient has loss of odor-producing glandular secretion in the axilla, but sweat production from widely distributed surface-opening glands remains normal. Which gland is affected?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the appendages of skin: hair follicles, glands, pilosebaceous units, arrector pili muscles.

options.rationale: Sebaceous glands release oily sebum and are usually follicle-associated. This would be correct if oily follicular secretion were absent.
Eccrine glands are widely distributed cooling glands that open onto the skin surface and remain functional here. This would be correct if generalized sweating were impaired.
Ceruminous glands are modified apocrine glands producing ear wax. This would be correct if secretion in the ear were absent.
Apocrine glands have limited distribution, including the axilla, and produce odor.
Mammary glands are modified apocrine glands producing milk. This would be correct if lactational secretion were affected.

question: A 52-year-old patient has reduced dermal strength, elasticity, tone, and texture after injury to the cells that produce collagen, elastic fibers, and reticular fibers. Which cells were damaged?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the following cells: keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans cells, Merkel cells, fibroblasts, and mast cells.

options.rationale: Keratinocytes produce keratin and form the protective epidermal barrier. This would be correct if epidermal keratinization were impaired.
Melanocytes synthesize melanin for pigmentation and ultraviolet protection. This would be correct if pigment production were lost.
Langerhans cells perform antigen presentation rather than produce dermal fibers. This would be correct if epidermal immune surveillance were impaired.
Mast cells release histamine during allergic responses rather than synthesize the dermal matrix. This would be correct if degranulation were impaired.
Fibroblasts produce dermal collagen, elastic fibers, and reticular fibers that contribute to skin strength, tone, and texture.

question: A 47-year-old patient loses insulation and structural padding after destruction of the deepest skin compartment. Histology would most likely show loss of which predominant tissue?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify skin layers: epidermis, dermis, subcutis.

options.rationale: The subcutis is composed mainly of mature adipose tissue, which provides insulation, fat storage, and structural padding.
Stratified squamous epithelium forms the epidermis rather than the deepest compartment. This would be correct if the external epithelial layer were destroyed.
Papillary dermis is superficial connective tissue contacting the epidermis. This would be correct if the superficial dermal layer were lost.
Reticular dermis is the deeper dermal layer contacting the subcutis but is not the predominantly adipose compartment. This would be correct if deep dermis were destroyed.
Cornified tissue forms the superficial stratum corneum. This would be correct if the outer protective keratin layer were lost.
